card.essence: Abrotanum is primarily indicated in marasmus (wasting) beginning in lower limbs and ascending, with paradoxical ravenous appetite yet progressive emaciation. Marked metastasis: symptoms shift from one location to another, notably rheumatism alternating with diarrhoea or haemorrhoids. Suppressed secretions (checked diarrhoea, skin eruptions) trigger serious sequelae—cardiac distress, rheumatic pain, bleeding. The patient is chilly, irritable, and presents with an old, wrinkled face despite youth.

keynotes.text: Marasmus beginning in lower extremities and ascending (opposite of Lycopodium)
Ravenous hunger with progressive emaciation despite eating well
Metastasis: rheumatism alternates with diarrhoea or haemorrhoids; mumps to testes
Suppressed secretions (diarrhoea, skin) followed by serious sequelae (cardiac, rheumatic)
Skin flabby, hangs loose in folds; face old, wrinkled, pale
Head weak, cannot hold it up (in marasmus)
Rheumatism: pain before swelling appears; from checked diarrhoea

modalities_worse.text: Checked secretions (diarrhoea, skin eruptions, other discharges)

mentals: Violent, inhuman; would like to do something cruel
physicals: Legs greatly emaciated; marasmus of lower extremities only
Stomach feels as if swimming in water, feels cold
Gnawing hunger and whining; food passes undigested
Haemorrhoids aggravated when rheumatism improves; bloody stools
Nosebleed, especially in boys and youths; hydrocele in boys
Joints stiff, swollen, lame; gout with pricking sensation in wrists and ankles
Very lame and sore all over; painful contraction of limbs
Back lame, weak, painful; neck so weak cannot hold head up
Itching chilblains; pricking and coldness in fingers and feet
Oozing from umbilicus (infants); bleeding from navel
Great weakness and prostration; hectic fever; unable to stand
Blue rings around dull-looking eyes; face old, pale, wrinkled
clinical: Marasmus in children with ascending emaciation (legs first, face last)
Tuberculous peritonitis; exudative pleurisy and processes
Post-operative chest pressure after hydrothorax or empyema drainage
Metastatic conditions: rheumatism following checked diarrhoea, mumps to testes/mammae
Cardiac symptoms following suddenly suppressed diarrhoea
Furuncles (after Hepar); pleurisy (after Aconite and Bryonia) with residual pressure

differentials.note: Both have ravenous hunger with emaciation and marasmus of legs, but Abrotanum has ascending wasting pattern and marked metastasis; Iodine more thyroid-related
Both marasmus with good appetite, skin hanging in folds (neck). Nat-m emaciation starts upper body; Abrot. starts lower limbs ascending
Both marasmus with flabby skin in folds and hunger. Sanicula has obstinate constipation; Abrotanum more diarrhoea-rheumatism alternation
Lycopodium emaciation descends (upper to lower); Abrotanum ascends (lower to upper). Both have good appetite with wasting
Both marasmus with emaciation of legs and ravenous hunger despite wasting. Tub. more respiratory focus; Abrot. more metastasis and rheumatic
Abrotanum follows Bryonia in pleurisy when pressing sensation persists impeding respiration. Abrot. has more metastasis and suppression sequelae
Both rheumatic with restlessness better motion. Abrot. rheumatism alternates with diarrhoea/piles, follows suppression; Rhus more ligamentous

cautions: Metastasis: watch for sudden shift of symptoms from one organ to another after suppression
Cardiac symptoms may follow abrupt cessation of diarrhoea or skin eruptions—requires prompt attention
